news.title: Gold Fields meets Black Challenge ahead of 2026 Amputee Football World Cup
news.lede: Gold Fields Ghana Limited has met with Ghana's amputee national football team, the Black Challenge, at the Mandiata Hotel in Accra to encourage the players ahead of the 2026 Amputee Football World Cup in Mexico. The meeting was attended by Ghana Football Association (GFA) President Kurt Okraku, National Paralympic Committee (NPC) President Samson Deen and other dignitaries. Gold Fields Ghana has committed US$500,000 to support the Black Challenge over a two-year period as part of its broader US$5 million sponsorship agreement with the GFA, which was unveiled on May 8, 2026. Speaking at the meeting, Gold Fields Ghana Vice President and Managing Director, Elliot Twum, encouraged the players to make the country proud and assured them of the company's continued support.

news.title: ‘An absolute afterthought’: the story of the Nigeria women’s team’s fall from grace
news.lede: The Super Falcons won’t be at the World Cup and with the prize money going up, they risk being left even further behind. It was a historic result in Casablanca – but not in a good way. Nigeria’s 2-1 defeat against South Africa in a playoff in August meant that the Super Falcons are missing out on the World Cup for the first time. It is a crushing blow for the most decorated national side in Africa across both men and women, one that has won no fewer than 10 Wafcon titles.

news.title: FIFA to share documents related to World Cup private investment plan
news.lede: PARIS FIFA will allow members of its ruling Council to view “key documents” related to the aborted project to sell stakes in the World Cup to private investors, a source close to world football’s governing body told AFP on Tuesday. “FIFA has informed the members of its Council, including all the vice-presidents, that they will have access to key documents in relation to FIFA Forward Enterprise,” the source told AFP, referring to FIFA president Gianni Infantino’s FFE proposal. Members of the Council -- a total of 37 people including Infantino and eight FIFA vice-presidents -- were informed on Monday in a letter sent by FIFA Secretary General Mattias Grafstrom that they must come forward “in the next two weeks” if they want to see the documents “in person and in specific conditions”.

news.title: FIFA opens access to abandoned World Cup stakes documents
news.lede: Members of FIFA’s ruling council will be given access to “key documents” on the scrapped plan to sell stakes in the World Cup to private investors, a source close to football’s world governing body told AFP on Tuesday. “FIFA has informed the members of its council, including all the vice-presidents, that they will have access to key documents in relation to FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE),” the source stated, referring to FIFA president Gianni Infantino’s FFE proposal. Members of the council, a total of 37 people including Infantino and eight FIFA vice-presidents, were informed on Monday in a letter sent by FIFA Secretary General Mattias Grafstrom that they must come forward “in the next two weeks” if they want to see the documents “in person and in specific conditions.”

news.title: How Asian Cup postponement will affect Europe’s big leagues as well as Gulf football
news.lede: The Asian Cup 2027 has been postponed because of the security situation in Saudi Arabia. The competition was set to take place from January 7 to February 5 next year, in eight venues across Riyadh, Jeddah and Khobar. It has been put back 11 months as a result of “exceptional circumstances arising from developments in the region”. It is now scheduled to start on December 23, 2027, with the final on January 21, 2028.

news.title: FIFA experiment with three new rules at under-15 World Cup that would change the sport forever
news.lede: In total, 4,505 goals were scored across 932 matches. FIFA made a series of bold changes at the under-15 World Cup, with three new rules being introduced to 'promote fast-paced football' and allow more touches of the ball. The inaugural under-15 World Cup & Festival took place in Azerbaijan last month, a tournament that featured 189 teams from six confederations: UEFA, CAF, AFC, CONCACAF, CONMEBOL and OFC. Spain were eventually crowned champions as goals from Tiago Polo, Bruno Fernandez and Adrian Bielsa sealed a 3-0 win over Czechia 3–0 in the Tier A final.

news.title: A Spectacular Football Celebration in Baku: FIFA U-15 World Cup and Festival Concludes
news.lede: Azerbaijan hosted another remarkable global tournament that has left a mark on its sports history – the FIFA U-15 World Cup and Festival. This prestigious event further solidified the country's position as a sports hub on the international stage, bringing together thousands of young talents from various countries in Baku. Teams from 189 FIFA member nations participated in the tournament, which featured nearly 1,000 matches. Organising and managing such large-scale global projects at a high level in our country requires significant sports diplomacy, hard work, and a strategic approach.
